NC-2025-HB747.aiSummary: North Carolina’s wildlife law changes became law. The act tightens privacy rules for some Wildlife Resources Commission records, creates new special license plates, and changes some boating safety and registration rules. It also lets the Wildlife Resources Commission sell one elk permit by raffle and one by auction for the 2027 hunting season, with the money going to elk conservation and management.

NC-2025-SB876.aiSummary: The act makes a range of local law changes in North Carolina. It changes how some Rowan County commissioner vacancies are filled, gives Rowan County special rules for taking over planning control from Kannapolis, and moves Kannapolis city elections to even-numbered years with partisan races for mayor and council. It also changes election rules and some vacancy rules for Albemarle and for several Moore County towns, including Aberdeen and Cameron, with some terms extended to match the new election dates.

NC-2025-HJR1243.aiSummary: The resolution would adjourn the North Carolina General Assembly on July 2, 2026, and bring it back on July 27, 2026, at noon. It would also limit what lawmakers may take up when they return, including budget bills, constitutional amendments, certain leftover 2025 bills and resolutions, and a few other listed matters. The resolution would take effect when it is ratified.

NC-2025-SB1057.aiSummary: The bill would set rules for proxy advisors, which are paid firms that tell shareholders how to vote on company matters. It would require them to say whether their advice against company management is or is not based on a written financial analysis, and to share that analysis on request when they have one. It would also require annual registration with the Secretary of State and a $100 fee. The act would take effect October 1, 2026, and apply to services provided on or after that date.

NC-2025-SB153.aiSummary: This law would let certain state law officers work with federal immigration agents under a formal agreement. It would also bar UNC schools from having rules that limit federal immigration law enforcement and from blocking the sharing of immigration-status information with federal law enforcement, to the extent federal law allows. It applies to UNC constituent institutions and state law enforcement, and it became law after a veto override.

NC-2025-HR1238.title: Honor 2026 Carolina Hurricanes Team.
NC-2025-HR1238.policyArea: AWARDS, HONORS & MEMORIALS; GENERAL ASSEMBLY; RESOLUTIONS, SIMPLE; SPORTS
NC-2025-HR1238.aiSummary: The North Carolina House resolution honors the Carolina Hurricanes for winning the 2026 Stanley Cup and for their strong 2025-2026 season. It also recognizes the team’s owner, management, and coach, and says the clerk must send certified copies to team members, owner Tom Dundon, and head coach Rod Brind'Amour. The resolution took effect when it was adopted.
